text:
Anthony Cirelli is the kind of player who makes the Lightning's numbers look right. When he's on the ice at five on five, Tampa takes 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 6.2 points better than when he sits. That's a two-way center doing his job at a level few in the league match, and Evolving-Hockey had him 95th percentile among forwards in driving play last season, with the caveat that he plays beside strong teammates.

His own scoring has run hot: 7 goals on 5 expected, a 20.6% shooting rate that sits well above his usual range. The flip side is bigger. Tampa has scored 7.1 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists. Those two things tend to meet in the middle, and his 16 points in 22 games could look about the same with the parts swapped.

He missed time earlier this month and returned November 17, and his minutes have dipped a little since. Two Stanley Cups in, he is 29 and still the player Jon Cooper trusts with the hard ones.
